Suggested time: 20 seconds.
You work for your money. Keeping track of it should not feel like a second job. Meet Finora: a personal finance project that connects everyday spending with a monthly plan.
Bridge: But first, a familiar magic trick.

Suggested time: 30 seconds.
Payday arrives and, for a moment, we all feel rich. Then come a coffee, a ride, another night out. Suddenly we are detectives trying to solve the case of our own missing money. The money did not vanish. We lost track of the small decisions behind the total.
Bridge: And the phrase that gets us into trouble? It’s only five dollars.
The disappearance and detective language are humorous exaggerations, not factual claims about user losses.

Suggested time: 30 seconds.
Five dollars sounds harmless. Repeat one extra five-dollar purchase for thirty days and the total reaches 150 dollars. This is an illustrative calculation, not a coffee price, customer average or promised saving. The point is how easily the monthly total can hide behind a small daily amount. Finora makes recorded spending visible so the user can decide whether that purchase is worth it.
Bridge: Now imagine that same blind spot inside a monthly budget.

Suggested time: 30 seconds.
Finora connects the everyday questions with clear answers. What did I spend? The transaction list shows the entries. Am I over budget? Category status shows the difference. How did the month go? The report explains the full picture. Users record their spending, and Finora brings those records together.
Bridge: First, the view we all want after payday: where do I stand?

Suggested time: 35 seconds.

In the sample month, recorded income is 5,250 dollars and expenses are 2,864 dollars. Their difference is 2,386 dollars, which the template calls monthly savings. This is the difference between recorded income and expenses, not proof of money held in a separate savings account. The dashboard image shows the intended prototype experience.

Transition to the next slide: That overview depends on the everyday entries behind it.

Users record an income or expense with an amount, date and category. The list keeps the entries together. Search and filters help find a transaction by month, type or category. Users can edit an incorrect entry or remove it. This makes it possible to trace a total back to its underlying purchases.

Transition to the next slide: Once the spending is recorded, Finora can compare it with the plan.

Suggested time: 40 seconds.

Return to the entertainment example. The budget is 200 dollars, and recorded spending is 225 dollars. Finora shows Exceeded and states that the category is 25 dollars over. Near-limit status appears from 80 percent through 100 percent, and spending above the limit is exceeded. The app reveals the situation so the user can review the next purchase. It does not guarantee savings or prevent spending.

Transition to the next slide: The next question is what the complete month tells us.

Suggested time: 35 seconds.

The report shows the spending categories for the selected month. Housing is the largest in this fictional example: 1,400 dollars, or 48.9 percent of total spending. This helps the user understand the pattern and review next month’s budget. The totals describe the recorded data and do not prescribe what someone should spend.

name: For people who want to actively track and review their spending.
text: A small habit today can make next month easier to understand.

Suggested time: 35 seconds.
Why bring Finora into your day? Because it gives a practical job to the numbers. Search helps you find the purchase behind a total. Budgets make your own limits visible. Editing and monthly review let the plan evolve with your life. You keep the choices. Finora supplies context.
Bridge: So, before we finish, one message from your money.

Your money called. It wants a game plan. Pause, smile, and ask: Ready to give it one? Invite the audience to try Finora with one expense, check the category budget, and see the monthly result.
No confirmed download or public demo URL was provided. The on-slide invitation directs people to the team demo. If asked about readiness: the main app has connected transactions, budgets and monthly reports. Dashboard and Income pages remain in progress. The standalone template resets on reload, and backend data resets on server restart.
